source.title: Sea Level Projections with Machine Learning Using Altimetry and Climate Models

claims.text: Satellite altimeter observations retrieved since 1993 show that the global mean sea level is rising at an unprecedented rate (3.4mm/year).
claims.claim_text: Satellite altimeter observations retrieved since 1993 show that the global mean sea level is rising at an unprecedented rate (3.4mm/year).

claims.text: This work presents a machine learning framework that exploits both satellite observations and climate model simulations to generate sea level rise projections at a 2-degree resolution spatial grid, 30 years into the future.
claims.claim_text: This work presents a machine learning framework that exploits both satellite observations and climate model simulations to generate sea level rise projections at a 2-degree resolution spatial grid, 30 years into the future.

claims.text: We propose segmenting our spatial dataset into meaningful clusters and show that clustering helps to improve predictions of our ML model.

claims.text: With almost three decades of observations, we can now investigate the contributions of anthropogenic climate-change signals such as greenhouse gases, aerosols, and biomass burning in this rising sea level.

claims.text: We use machine learning (ML) to investigate future patterns of sea level change.

claims.text: To understand the extent of contributions from the climate-change signals, and to help in forecasting sea level change in the future, we turn to climate model simulations.

claims.text: Through our work, we show the potential of machine learning in producing these forecasts 30 years in advance and over all oceans at a reasonably good spatial resolution.
